name: Jan van Eyck
bio: Pioneer of oil painting technique in Northern Europe; renowned for the Ghent Altarpiece and the Arnolfini Portrait, both celebrated for their minute realism and use of light.

name: Robert Campin
bio: Often identified as the 'Master of Flémalle'; an early Netherlandish painter whose workshop is thought to have trained both Rogier van der Weyden and Jacques Daret.

name: Rogier van der Weyden
bio: Leading Early Netherlandish painter known for emotionally intense religious compositions, most famously the Descent from the Cross.

name: Hans Memling
bio: German-born painter who worked in Bruges; known for serene portraits and devotional panels that softened the intensity of his predecessors.

name: Dieric Bouts
bio: Early Netherlandish painter noted for his early use of single-point perspective and calm, restrained figures.

name: Petrus Christus
bio: Bruges-based painter who furthered the use of linear perspective in Netherlandish painting, likely influenced directly by van Eyck's workshop.

name: Hieronymus Bosch
bio: Highly original painter of fantastical, moralizing religious allegory; best known for The Garden of Earthly Delights.

name: Hugo van der Goes
bio: Ghent-based painter celebrated for the Portinari Altarpiece, whose emotional intensity influenced Italian painters who saw it after its export to Florence.

name: Gerard David
bio: Bruges painter working at the close of the Early Netherlandish tradition, known for luminous landscapes and devotional works.

name: Albrecht Dürer
bio: Widely considered the greatest artist of the German Renaissance; painter, printmaker, and theorist who bridged Northern detail with Italian ideas of proportion and perspective.

name: Lucas Cranach the Elder
bio: Court painter closely associated with the Reformation and Martin Luther, known for portraits and mythological/allegorical nudes.

name: Hans Holbein the Younger
bio: German portraitist best known for his precise, psychologically penetrating portraits of the English royal court under Henry VIII.

name: Matthias Grünewald
bio: Painter of the Isenheim Altarpiece, notable for its raw emotional intensity and unconventional use of color and distortion.

name: Albrecht Altdorfer
bio: Regensburg painter and printmaker, among the earliest European artists to treat landscape as an independent subject.

name: Pieter Bruegel the Elder
bio: Flemish painter renowned for landscapes and scenes of peasant life, including Hunters in the Snow and The Harvesters.

name: Quentin Matsys
bio: Antwerp painter credited with founding the Antwerp school of painting, known for blending Netherlandish tradition with emerging Italian influence.

name: Joachim Patinir
bio: Early specialist in landscape painting, often subordinating religious figures to sweeping, fantastical panoramas.

name: Jean Fouquet
bio: Leading French painter and manuscript illuminator of the 15th century, court painter to Charles VII and Louis XI.

name: Jean Clouet
bio: Court painter to Francis I of France, known for his portraits combining Netherlandish precision with French courtly elegance.
